newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia seeks World Bank loan to restructure banks.
newsitem.headline: Russia seeks World Bank loan to restructure banks.

text.p: Russia's central bank and finance ministry are working on raising a $1 billion loan from the World Bank to restructure Russia's banking system, a top central banker said on Tuesday.
"Banking system restructuring is the central bank's and government's priority," first deputy chairman Alexander Khandruyev told a banking conference.
Russia would use the credit to restructure commercial bank balances, create a system of household deposit insurance and set up an agency to manage the assets of bankrupt banks, he said.
Many Russian banks are in a difficult financial situation with every fourth bank working at a loss, Khandruyev said.
Many banks were on the verge of bankruptcy as a result of a risky credit policy, he said.

The central bank withdrew 161 licences or liquidated about six percent of currently active banks in the first seven months of this year, Khandruyev said in a statement. In 1995 the central bank withdrew 225 licences.
The number of active banks shrunk to 2,119 on July 8, 1996, from 2,132 on June 1 and 2,263 on February 1, 1996, central bank figures show.
